html:
SMTO-PSM-0007 — Parameter Store is disabled

GUID: a6a02082-b6e3-4f35-ba42-0caaaf93dba8
Slug: parameter-disabled
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • Your request uses a saved parameter with @, but saved parameters are switched off or not available on this SMTO server. SMTO paused the task before starting it, so nothing has run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you didn't mean to use a saved parameter, select Use as literal text in the message under your request. This sends the @ words as ordinary text, so the task can start without Parameter Store (the place SMTO keeps saved details like server addresses and passwords).
  2. If you do need the saved parameter, ask the person who manages SMTO to turn Parameter Store on in the server's startup settings and restart the server. This server has Parameter Store turned off or couldn't start it, and only someone who manages the server can change that.
  3. Once they confirm it is on, select Check again under your request. Check again looks up your @ references again now that Parameter Store is available.

What success looks like

  • The message under your request says the references were resolved, and the task starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If you don't need the task, select Cancel task; nothing has run yet.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The prompt contains @ parameter references, but reference resolution is disabled (agent_parameter_store_enabled is false) or the runtime has no Parameter Store instance, so the task is held before inference.

What this means

  • A prompt contains parameter references but resolution is disabled or has no store instance. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • A prompt contains parameter references but resolution is disabled or has no store instance.

How to diagnose it

  • Check effective Parameter Store enablement and runtime service availability separately.

How to fix it

  • Check AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_STORE_ENABLED (setting agent_parameter_store_enabled, default true) in the Server's startup environment; set it to true and restart the Server. If it is already enabled, the runtime has no parameter_store instance: check the Server log for Parameter Store initialization errors at agent_parameters_db_path. Then choose Check again on the held task.
  • Enable the intended Parameter Store through its supported controls, or remove the unresolved reference from the new task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported store is available or the new task deliberately removes its unresolved reference.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
